summary: A Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Ryoshin Nakao served at the Research Institute of Soto Zen Buddhism and Hanazono University, where he was a professor (attested 1998) and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Ryosho Hayashi studied at Taisho University and Tokyo Metropolitan University. He served as professor (1975), Dean of Letters (1981), and professor emeritus (1990–1994) at Taisho University, and chaired the Japan-DPRK Cultural Exchange Association (1990).

Ryosho Nakamura is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Seventh Higher School Zoshikan, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, and Rissho University. He served as a professor at The International University of Kagoshima from circa 1970 to 1998.

A Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Ryosho Tanaka held several roles there, including professor (2002–2003) and president (2009). He also served as professor at Ryukoku University and director of the Sōtō Zen Center for Advanced Studies (2005).

Ryoshu Koda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. He held researcher positions at Taisho University (attested 1998) and the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 2006).

Ryoshu Michihata worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After studying at Otani University, he held a post there from circa 1934 to 1969, and later served as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University from circa 1969 to 1978.
Ryoshu Misaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and later served there as professor emeritus (attested 1988–2000).

A Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University, Ryoshun Okubo served as Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism there (circa 2005). He also held posts at Taimon Kenkyūkai (attested 2007), ICPBS (attested 2026), and IIBS (attested 2026).

Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Ryudo Fujii studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. His career includes posts at JSPS (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).

Ryugen Tanemura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held teaching posts at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013) and Taisho University (attested 2014–2026), and served as a researcher at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).

Ryuhiko Taga, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Rissho University (~1953–1955). He spent his academic career there, advancing from lecturer (~1961–1967) and associate professor (~1967–1974) to professor (~1974–2002) and president (~1992–1995).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, Ryuichi Abe studied at Keio, SAIS/Johns Hopkins, Taisho, and Columbia. He taught at Columbia (1991–2004) before becoming Edwin O. Reischauer Institute Professor of Japanese Religions at Harvard (~2003).

Ryuji Hayashi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Delhi. He has held posts at Tohoku University, NIT Sendai College, Eastern Institute, and Kodomo Kyoiku Hosen College, where he was professor (attested 2015).

Ryujo Yamada worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, studying under Sylvain Lévi. He served as professor (attested 1953) and professor emeritus (attested 1972–1973) at Tohoku University, and as head of Musashino University (attested 1963).

Ryuken Nawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He serves as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Ryuken Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Ryuo was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Tō-ji (Tō-ji Sōgaku) and at Koyasan University.
Ryusei Keira is a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Tom Tillemans at the University of Lausanne, completing his thesis in 2003.
Ryushin Kitao is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a professor at Shuchiin University (attested 2014 and 2026).
Ryushin Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a professorship at Bukkyo University (attested 2015) and serves as a faculty member at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
